summary: Given disjoint segments [l, r] each with c coins per position, pick k consecutive positions to maximise total coins.
mainInsight: An optimal window can be assumed to start at the left end of some segment or end at the right end of some segment (otherwise slide it to gain or break even). Sort the segments and sweep twice, keeping the sum of fully covered segments plus a partial edge segment.

approaches.name: Sort + prefix sums + binary search
approaches.summary: For each aligned window, binary-search the edge segment using prefix sums of full-segment totals.

approaches.name: Sort + two sliding-window sweeps
approaches.summary: Sweep with the window starting at each segment's left end, then mirror with windows ending at each right end; keep full-segment sum + partial edge.
strengths: No binary search or prefix array

personalSolution.approach: Sort + two sliding-window sweeps (start-aligned and end-aligned)
personalSolution.notes: Optimal. Your comments show the bug you fixed by adding the second sweep - a good thing to remember.

cards.answer: Sort the segments and sweep a window that starts at some segment's left end (and mirror it for right ends), tracking covered coins. Clue: Bags come as weighted intervals on a huge line and you choose k consecutive positions, so the best window can be aligned to an interval's edge; sort the intervals and slide a window over them.
keyPoints: Bags come as weighted intervals on a huge line and you choose k consecutive positions, so the best window can be aligned to an interval's edge; sort the intervals and slide a window over them.
cards.explanation: Sliding a window that is not aligned to an edge never improves the total, so only edge-aligned windows need to be evaluated.

promptVariants: What is the key observation that reduces the candidate windows?
Which windows need to be considered?
options: Windows that start at a segment's left end or end at its right end
Every integer start position between the first and last segment
Only windows centred on the largest segment of the whole array
Windows starting at index 0 and ending only at the last cell
cards.answer: Windows that start at a segment's left end or end at its right end
cards.explanation: If neither end is aligned with a segment boundary, sliding the window one step either way changes the total linearly, so one direction is never worse until an end aligns.

promptVariants: Why can the optimal window be assumed aligned with a segment boundary?
cards.answer: Between boundaries the window's coin total changes linearly as it slides (each step adds the density at one end and removes the density at the other). A linear function on an interval is maximised at an endpoint, i.e. when an end of the window hits a segment boundary. So only boundary-aligned windows need checking.
keyPoints: Total is piecewise linear while sliding
cards.explanation: This is why two sweeps (start-aligned, end-aligned) suffice.

promptVariants: Sorting dominates, so the algorithm runs in ___ time.
cards.explanation: Sort O(n log n); each sweep is linear.

promptVariants: What is the extra space and what trade-off does it show against the prefix-sum solution?
Compare the extra memory of the two-sweep solution with a prefix-sum + binary-search solution.
cards.answer: O(1) extra besides sorting; the prefix-sum + binary-search solution uses O(n) space and an extra log factor.

promptVariants: In the left-to-right sweep what are `fullSum`, `rightBound` and `edge`, and why is the full-bag sum reduced at the end of each iteration?
How does the sweep handle a partially covered last segment?
cards.code:
rightBound = coins[i][0] + k
while j + 1 < n and coins[j + 1][0] < rightBound:
    lj, rj, cj = coins[j]
    fullSum += (rj - lj + 1) * cj
    j += 1
edge = 0
if j < n and coins[j][0] < rightBound:
    lj, rj, cj = coins[j]
    edge += min(rj - lj + 1, rightBound - lj) * cj
best = max(best, fullSum + edge)
fullSum -= (coins[i][1] - coins[i][0] + 1) * coins[i][2]
cards.answer: The window starts at coins[i][0] and covers [start, start + k). fullSum accumulates segments entirely inside the window before the last one; the last overlapping segment is the edge, contributing only min(its length, covered part) * c. After evaluating, segment i is removed from fullSum because the next window starts at segment i + 1.
cards.explanation: The mirrored sweep handles windows ending at a right boundary.

promptVariants: Why are two sweeps (left-to-right and right-to-left) needed?
Which window shape does the second sweep cover?
options: The best window may start at a left end or end at a right end
The array may not be sorted, so both orders are required here
To handle overlapping segments by merging them all up front
To avoid integer overflow in the running total of the window
cards.answer: The best window may start at a left end or end at a right end
cards.explanation: A window ending at a right boundary is not necessarily starting at any left boundary, so both orientations must be tried.
